land.text: central Ulster round Armagh, taken from the Ulaid by the Three Collas (infobox: preceded by Ulaid); the fall of Emain Macha is dated 450 in a tradition on the Ulaid page
'Rossa Boy MacMahon agreed to surrender and regrant his lands to the English Crown'; the territory became County Monaghan

correction.text: Airgíalla at its peak, which 'roughly matched the modern dioceses of Armagh and Clogher': parts of Armagh, Monaghan, Louth, Fermanagh, Tyrone and Londonderry (drawn as Armagh, Monaghan, Fermanagh and Louth; the Tyrone and Londonderry parts belong to the Tír Eoghain shape)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Airgíalla. The page gives the peak 'in the 12th century, under king Donnchad Ua Cerbaill' (1130-1168) and no area; the extent is the diocese reading. The infobox start is 331 ('around 331' for the battle of Achadh Leithdheirg, a tale the page calls 'mostly fiction'); 450 is the Ulaid page's other tradition for the fall of Emain Macha, used so that the two shapes do not overlap.

correction.text: the surviving Monaghan portion, 'Oirghialla', under the Mac Mathghamhna 'until the end of the Gaelic order in Ireland'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; the Louth portion 'became known as Uriel after the Anglo-Norman invasion' and the Monaghan portion survived. The page gives no date for the change; 1189 is the end of Murchard Ua Cerbaill's reign on the king list (1168-1189), so a bridge. The page says nothing about Armagh, Fermanagh and the Tyrone fringe after the invasion.

region.text: central Ulster taken from the Ulaid by the Three Collas

ledger.note: The Three Collas 'supposedly took much of central Ulster from the Ulaid'; the battle of Achadh Leithdheirg is dated 'around 331' (infobox 'Established: 331'), the victors killed Fergus Foga and burned Emain Macha; the page calls this 'mostly fiction' and says the actual year and circumstances are unknown. 450 is the Ulaid page's other tradition ('dated the fall of Emain Macha to 450 AD'), used to match the Ulaid dossier's loss (confidence 1).

region.text: Airgíalla, vassal of the Cenél nEógain

ledger.note: [Reviewer eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] Mirror of tir-eoghain's 827 vassal_start. 'From 735 they fell under the dominance of the Cenél nEógain, and by 827 had become their vassals' (Airgíalla page).

region.text: Airgíalla, independent again under Donnchad Ua Cerbaill

ledger.note: [Reviewer eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] Mirror of tir-eoghain's 1130 vassal_end, a bridge: the page gives no end to the vassalage, only that the kingdom 'was at its peak in the 12th century, under king Donnchad Ua Cerbaill' (king list 1130-1168/1169).

region.text: Armagh and Fermanagh, left out of the surviving Oirghialla

ledger.note: Page silent on a date and on who took them: after the Norman invasion only the Monaghan portion 'survived' as Oirghialla and the Ua Cerbaill line on the king list ends with Muirchertach (1189-1194). From 735 the Airgíalla had fallen under the Cenél nEógain (see tir-eoghain); 1189 is a bridge.

'The Louth portion became known as Uriel after the Anglo-Norman invasion.' The page gives no year and no Norman lord; 1189 is a bridge (confidence 1). The Lordship of Ireland dossier has no matching gain.

1585: the kingdom ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: 1585'; the main text says it 'came to an end in 1585' when Rossa Boy MacMahon agreed to 'surrender and regrant' his lands to the English Crown; the territory became County Monaghan. The king list runs on to Hugh Roe McMahon (1589-1590); the page does not call 1590 the end.

certainty.note: The page names dioceses and counties, no frontier.

sources.title: Airgíalla
sources.note: Identity, Three Collas, 735/827 Cenél nEógain domination, Ua Cerbaill peak, Louth and Monaghan, 1585.

notes: Slug follows the ulaid dossier's counterpart 'airgialla'. The page gives no capital ('Armagh and Clogher' are its main towns). From 735 the Airgíalla 'fell under the dominance of the Cenél nEógain, and by 827 had become their vassals' (the vassal pair is recorded in tir-eoghain, as the overlord's dossier). The 700 loss in the ulaid dossier (all Ulster west of the Bann, counterpart airgialla) is wider than the Airgíalla shape: the rest of that land is Cenél nEógain's and is in tir-eoghain; no mirror gain is written here for it. King list: Colla Uais (331-?), Donnchad Ua Cerbaill 1130-1168/9, Murchard 1168-1189, Muirchertach 1189-1194, Eochaid mac Mathgahamna d. 1273 ... Rossa mac Maghnusa 1497-1513, Rossa Buidhe 1579-1585 (infobox; the king list says to 1589). The early records (Dunchad mac Ultan 677, Mael Fothataig 697) are not territorial. The page budget was one page.
